text: Topics and partitions were introduced in Lesson 2. This lesson is about how a producer actually decides which partition a message lands on — a real design decision, not a formality.
With a key, Kafka hashes it and that key always lands on the same partition, guaranteeing per-key ordering. Without a key, Kafka spreads round-robin: even load, no ordering guarantee.

Partition count bounds parallelism directly. Too few, and extra consumers just sit idle. Too many, and every partition is real overhead — more file handles, slower rebalances, more replication traffic.
The hashing only spreads load evenly if key values are even. Key by country and one partition can take ninety percent of the load. Key by customer ID and it spreads naturally.
Partition count and key choice directly determine your ordering guarantees and where bottlenecks show up later. Next up: retention — how long a message actually sticks around.
